TestSimple::test_simple_single_node_writ.description: Smoke test: start a 1-node cluster with --smp 1 / --smp 2 (params), write 100k rows with cassandra-stress (native cql3, seq=1..100000, 1 thread), read them back with c-s and assert the output has no 'Data returned was not validated' and no 'Exception' (validate_stress_output, simple_no_driver_test.py:47-67). c-s non-zero exit also fails via ccm ToolError (scylla-ccm/ccmlib/node.py:2179). Guards basic single-node write/read path and c-s/java-driver compatibility; no specific scylla bug. One of the first Scylla dtests ('Enable urchin').

origin.summary: Shlomi Livne: simple tests to validate single node/cluster is working (500k rows, 10 threads)

TestSimple::test_simple_single_node_writ.reason: Pure smoke test (1 node, c-s write+read, smp 1/2); scenario implicitly exercised by cqlpy (test_cql_query.py::test_cassandra_stress_like_write_and_read) and by many c-s-using dtests, but it is a cheap explicit c-s compatibility gate - keep vs remove is a gating-policy call. Bug: start_rpc=true (simple_no_driver_test.py:22) is dead since thrift removal (scylladb ad649be1bf, start_rpc Unused). Note: read uses '-mode cql3 simplenative' while write uses 'native cql3' (73444cf8 only changed write); prepare() docstring says '3 CCM Nodes' but test uses 1; `type(cluster) is ScyllaCluster` branch always true.
